name: EchoStar
description: EchoStar is the holding company that owns DISH satellite TV, Sling streaming TV, Boost Mobile wireless and Hughes satellite broadband. Pay-TV (about 7.0 million US subscribers at end-2025) pays for itself with monthly subscriptions and is the only profitable segment; Boost Mobile (7.5 million subscribers) loses money and now rides AT&T's network as a hybrid carrier. Having built a 5G network, it abandoned it in 2025 after the FCC questioned its spectrum use, and agreed to sell spectrum licences to AT&T (closed 2026-07-28 for $20.25B cash) and to SpaceX (about $20B, mostly SpaceX stock, with the final closing targeted for 2027-11-30). Two of its subsidiary groups filed a prepackaged Chapter 11 on 2026-06-30.

businessLines.name: Pay-TV (DISH TV and Sling TV)
businessLines.how: Monthly subscription fees from households for a TV package (satellite or internet-streamed), less programming costs paid to content owners; shrinking as customers cut the cord.
businessLines.description: DISH satellite TV (5.022M subscribers) and Sling streaming TV (1.976M) at 2025-12-31; also receivers and broadcast services for third parties.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating income; share of total is not meaningful because consolidated operating income was a $17.7B loss; vs $2,648.0M FY2024

businessLines.name: Wireless (Boost Mobile, Gen Mobile)
businessLines.how: Monthly prepaid and postpaid phone plans plus device sales; pays AT&T and T-Mobile per-use network fees under long-term agreements, so margin is the plan price minus those fees and device subsidies.
businessLines.description: 7.511M wireless subscribers at 2025-12-31; since 2025-11-15 operates a 'Hybrid MNO' (own core network, AT&T supplies radio network through 2031) plus a T-Mobile MVNO agreement.

businessLines.name: Broadband and Satellite Services (Hughes)
businessLines.how: Monthly subscriptions from rural consumers, plus multi-year contracts for satellite capacity, gateway and terminal equipment sold to airlines, governments and enterprises.
businessLines.description: HughesNet consumer satellite internet (739,000 subscribers), plus satellite networks, terminals and in-flight connectivity for enterprise, airline and government customers.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating loss after Q3-Q4 2025 impairments and other charges; FY2024 loss $117.9M

businessLines.name: Other (legacy 5G network)
businessLines.how: Little: carrying cost of network and spectrum; value is realised when licences are sold (AT&T and SpaceX deals) rather than from operations.
businessLines.description: The terminated 5G network build and the spectrum licences being sold; separated from Wireless in the FY2025 10-K.

operatingProfit.note: Mostly non-cash impairments of the abandoned 5G network and spectrum ($17.632B total impairment and other charges across segments in Q3-Q4 2025); FY2024 loss $2,353.9M

brands.note: Primary wireless brand; 7.511M wireless subscribers across Boost and Gen Mobile
